title: Resource Models and Loading

# Resource Models and Loading

RECAP exposes lightweight references and hydrated schemas so callers can choose
between identity-oriented queries and complete resource trees.

## Reference and full models

Reference models contain identity and scalar fields without loading children,
properties, or other relationships. Full models contain the schema needed for
relationship access.

```python
references = (
    namespace.query_maker()
    .resources(shape="ref")
    .filter(name="Sample Plate 001")
    .all()
)

plates = (
    namespace.query_maker()
    .resources(shape="full", load="none")
    .include(["template", "properties"])
    .all()
)
```

Use `load="eager"` when the complete relationship tree is required. For a
resource query, eager loading materializes the entire child subtree with a
bounded number of database statements. It can still materialize more data than
needed, so targeted descendant queries are preferable when only one level or
template is relevant.

## Property model access

Resources created through builders expose property access models directly. A
resource loaded with `include(["properties"])` may require
`build_property_model()` before accessing nested values. Process-run queries
using `include_resources()` hydrate assigned resources and their children for
property access.

```python
for resource in plates:
    resource.build_property_model()
    print(resource.properties.dimensions.rows.value)
```

## Child resources

```python
plate = namespace.query_maker().resources(load="eager").first()
well = plate.children["A01"]

for name, child in plate.children.items():
    print(name, child.id)
```

Child hierarchies can be defined in a template or extended at runtime through a
resource builder. Child identity remains scoped by its parent while the root
resource retains its own UUID.
